title: What Actually Matters: Startups, Capital, and the Rules Nobody Taught Us
description: Nobody explained how this actually works. Not for the founder who took 150 meetings to get one check. Not for the angel who wrote $25K into a friend's startup and can't sleep wondering if they just lit it on fire. Not for the GP who spent two years raising a fund while working a day job because it was the only option. Not for the LP who backed a fund with a Goldman pedigree and watched it return less than 1x. Not for the ecosystem builder who runs the infrastructure everyone depends on and nobody pays for. The venture capital system wasn't built to explain itself. Lolita Taub wrote What Actually Matters: Startups, Capital, and the Rules Nobody Taught Us because she got tired of watching people figure it out alone. What's inside: How startup fundraising and angel investing actually work and why most investor "no"s have nothing to do with you What SAFEs, term sheets, and side letters quietly decide about your cap table and ownership How to spot a zombie fund before you pitch it (includes the Zombie Fund Detection Script) How LP/GP fund structure works from the inside and what emerging managers need before they have a track record When raising helps, and when it hurts - the full funding spectrum including non-dilutive options How ecosystem building and community replace pedigree when you build it right How to stay in the game for a decade without burning yourself to the ground AI prompts you paste directly into ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini to pressure-test your specific situation in real time Who this is for: First-time founders raising startup capital without warm intros Angels writing early checks and learning what information rights and pro rata actually protect Emerging managers building a pre-seed or seed venture fund from scratch LPs trying to figure out which GPs

title: The 20% That Actually Matters: A beginner's guide to health that works in real life
description: Getting healthier shouldn’t require rebuilding your entire life. The 20% That Actually Matters is a practical guide to the small number of health choices that create the greatest return. Instead of chasing perfect routines, complicated diets, and temporary bursts of motivation, you’ll learn how to build habits that can survive busy schedules, low-energy days, missed workouts, takeout dinners, and real life. Inside, you’ll discover how to: Simplify healthy eating without giving up foods you enjoy Make movement and strength training fit an imperfect schedule Improve sleep without creating an elaborate nightly production Use normal and minimum versions of important habits Recover from missed days without starting over Identify the routines that deserve your time and attention The included Core 20% Companion walks you through a practical audit, helps you choose your highest-value habits, and turns them into a flexible one-page health plan. You do not need a perfect routine. title: Easy Hard vs. Hard Hard: Finding the Work That Actually Matters to You
description: Are you exhausted from working hard but still feeling unfulfilled? Most of us have been taught that the answer to unhappiness is simple: work harder, grind longer, and push through. But what if the real problem isn’t how hard you work; it’s what you’re working on ? In Easy Hard vs. Hard Hard , Dr. Robert H. Shelton introduces a powerful new way of thinking about effort, fulfillment, and purpose. Drawing from his own transformation of losing nearly 180 pounds, battling burnout, earning a doctorate in leadership, and learning to lead himself before leading others, Dr. Shelton lays out a framework that will help you stop chasing the wrong goals and finally start living a life that feels like yours. At the heart of the book are two types of work: Easy Hard : These are the tasks that keep you busy, stressed, and constantly seeking approval. They might impress others, but they drain you. Promotions, accolades, and routines that look good on paper. Hard Hard : This is the work that matters to you . It’s difficult, yes, but deeply meaningful. It requires courage, self-leadership, and persistence. And while it may not earn applause, it builds real satisfaction, growth, and peace. Through a blend of research, real-life stories, and practical exercises, you’ll learn how to: Recognize the signs of misaligned work that lead to burnout, procrastination, and loss of purpose. Shift from chasing external validation to pursuing goals rooted in your deepest values. Develop tools for self-assessment, self-monitoring, and sustainable action. Replace busyness with progress, and exhaustion with the good kind of tired—the kind that comes from building something meaningful. Dr. Shelton doesn’t just offer theory; he offers a roadmap. title: Integrity @ Work 2.0 What Actually Matters: Leveling Up To Wealth That Means Something
description: The most meaningful shift in your relationship with money may come when you stop asking, How do I grow this? and start asking, What is this actually for? You've worked hard. You've made sacrifices. You've built something real. And yet, there comes a time when having enough isn't quite enough. That wondering isn't a problem. It's a door. On the other side is a different way of thinking about wealth. One that isn't defined only by what you've accumulated, but by what your money makes possible. More time with the people you love. Experiences that become part of who you are. The freedom to take care of yourself, contribute to something that matters, and leave behind more than a financial inheritance. The true meaning of wealth isn't found on a balance sheet. It's found in the life that wealth allows you to create. Integrity @ Work 2.0 is an invitation to put your life back at the center of your financial plan and begin thinking about your money not only in terms of what you have, but what you want it to mean. You've already done the work. title: Overdo What Matters: How to Stop Wasting Your Intensity and Start Giving Your Best Energy
description: You already have the intensity. You just haven't decided where it goes. You can worry for two hours about a conversation that will be forgotten in two weeks. You can become an accidental expert in a hobby you don't even care about. You can spend a Sunday comparing your life to strangers you've never met — all while the manuscript, the marriage, the skill that could change the next twenty years sits untouched. The problem was never a lack of discipline. It's that your discipline keeps showing up for the wrong assignment. Overdo What Matters makes an uncomfortable case: whatever is actually worth doing is worth overdoing — not recklessly, not at the cost of your health or your sanity, but with the same disproportionate, relentless care you already give to things that will be forgotten by Thursday. Inside, you'll find: A real method for identifying what actually matters to you — not what you'd say at a dinner party The difference between purposeful excellence and anxious perfectionism, and how to tell which one you're bringing A complete system — the Reallocation Cycle — for redirecting wasted intensity toward what compounds A working plan you build by the final chapter, not just an idea you'll admire and forget You are going to spend your intensity somewhere. This book won't ask you for more of it. It will help you finally aim the intensity you've already got.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstanceM0DPRMKAlBJwft3MwwSAcw')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-fil

title: UNPLUG & RISE: The NLP Blueprint to Break Free from Social Media Addiction, Reclaim Your M
description: UNPLUG & RISE — Book Summary NLP Blueprint for Social Media Freedom The Core Premise Social media addiction is not a personal weakness — it is a neurological pattern engineered by tech platforms using behavioral psychology, variable rewards, and infinite scroll systems similar to slot machines. This book exposes that design and provides NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) tools to break free, helping readers build a life so meaningful that no algorithm can compete. Part One — Understanding the Trap The book begins with the neuroscience behind addiction. Dopamine is not pleasure but anticipation — it drives the urge before the reward. Notifications, likes, and scrolling reinforce this loop. Three key cycles sustain addiction: Social validation (need for approval) Information anxiety (fear of missing out) Boredom avoidance (inability to stay still) Over time, the brain changes in ways similar to substance addiction. The costs are severe: lost time, weakened relationships, reduced focus, identity distortion, poor sleep, and physical strain. The SCROLL test (Salience, Control, Relief, Obligations, Lying, Loss) helps readers assess their dependency honestly. Part Two — The NLP Toolkit Seven NLP techniques form the action plan: Pattern Interrupt breaks compulsive habits. Swish Pattern replaces triggers with empowering self-images. Anchoring creates instant access to strong emotional states. Reframing changes how scrolling is perceived. Meta Model challenges mental excuses. Timeline Therapy addresses emotional roots. Future Pacing builds a vision of a free self. The key insight: lasting change requires identity transformation. When you see yourself as someone who doesn’t need validation, the addiction weakens. But underneath, something is beginning to crack-and no amount of success, performance, or achievement seems to fix it. Josh Wintermute knows that feeling well. In this honest and practical book, Josh walks you through the three foundational areas every life is built on-your heart, your home, and your culture. He helps you uncover what's broken beneath the surface, do the hard work of restoration, and rebuild on what truly matters. You are not as stuck as you think. You are not as alone as you feel. title: Baby Gear That Matters: What You Actually Need (and What You Don’t)
description: Navigating the world of baby gear can feel overwhelming. From endless “must, have” lists to the newest gadgets promising to make life easier, parents often find themselves buried under products they don’t actually need. Baby Gear That Matters: What You Actually Need (and What You Don’t) is the essential guide for new and seasoned parents who want clarity, confidence, and practicality when outfitting their nursery and daily routines. This book cuts through the noise, helping you focus on the items that truly make caring for your baby simpler, safer, and more enjoyable.Inside, you’ll discover which products are genuinely worth your time, money, and space, and which are overrated extras that create clutter without real benefit. Learn how to set up a functional nursery that supports feeding, sleep, diapering, and play without unnecessary gadgets. Explore practical advice for on, the, go gear, bath time, and sleep essentials, along with tips for streamlining daily routines. Each recommendation is grounded in real, world parenting experience, balancing safety, convenience, and affordability so you can feel confident in your choices.This book also addresses the subtle pressures of modern parenting, including marketing tactics, peer influence, and the temptation to buy every trendy item. With clear, approachable guidance, it empowers you to make decisions based on your family’s unique needs, lifestyle, and space. No more second, guessing, overbuying, or wasting time with items that offer little value. Instead, you’ll gain insight into what truly supports you and your baby during those first critical months and beyond.Whether you’re a first, time parent or adding another child to your family, Baby Gear That Matters equips you with the tools to make smart, confident choices. description: First trip to Korea without the frozen what do I say now moment? This compact, situation-first guide adds cultural context that helps a phrase land well. Inside: ready-to-say phrases for food, transport, shopping, lodging, and help; Hangul, readable pronunciation, concise translations; quick etiquette notes; screen-friendly phrase cards; and a calm-plan checklist for your first 48 hours in Korea.
